stem:
Aarav writes $48 = 12 \times 4$ and $90 = 15 \times 6$. He asks whether that single pair of factorisations proves that $48$ and $90$ have no common factor other than $1$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Yes, because those written factor pairs show no matching factor on the page.
No, because another factorisation can still reveal a common factor such as $6$.
An incomplete factor listing is what creates the claim that the numbers share a factor.
The same single-pair check also settles every later prime-factorisation question about these numbers.

teacher.key_rationale: One chosen factorisation can miss a shared factor. Here $48=6\times8$ and $90=6\times15$, so $6$ is common. Matching factors on one writing is not a full search. The incomplete listing does not create the shared factor. A single pair does not replace full prime-factor work.
